in-pusiostoma-mendicaria.title: Bumble Bee Snail
in-pusiostoma-mendicaria.sci: Pusiostoma mendicaria (also listed as Engina mendicaria)
in-pusiostoma-mendicaria.summary: A tiny black-and-yellow banded snail that scavenges leftovers and burrows in the sand.
rows: About 1-1/2 in; Wikipedia gives a shell of 10–20 mm (0.4–0.8 in)
Carnivore scavenger. Uneaten meaty food, decaying matter and small sand worms
Red Sea and Indian Ocean across the tropical Indo-Pacific to northern Australia

in-nassarius-sp.title: Nassarius Snail
in-nassarius-sp.summary: A burrowing scavenger snail that pops out of the sand, siphon first, when it smells food.
rows: Carnivore scavenger. Leftover food, detritus and decaying matter
notes: Lives buried in the sand with only its siphon showing; needs a sand bed.
Works well in a small group.

in-astraea-tecta.title: Star Turbo Snail (Astraea Snail)
in-astraea-tecta.summary: A cone-shelled grazing snail that cleans algae off live rock.
rows: About 1 in; wild record 6 cm (2.4 in) DL (SeaLifeBase)
Herbivore. Film and hair algae on rocks and glass

in-conomurex-luhuanus.title: Strawberry Conch
in-conomurex-luhuanus.summary: A sand-sifting conch with an orange lip. Also sold as Orange Lip or Tiger Conch. It moves with a hopping motion.
rows: About 3 in; wild record 8 cm (3.1 in) SHL (SeaLifeBase)
Omnivore. Algae and detritus on the sand bed
notes: Needs a sand bed to forage in.
